walkthroughs.body_html:
An Introduction to Christian Ethics — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

An Introduction to Christian Ethics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with An Introduction to Christian Ethics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the second formulation about?
options: Universalisability
Humanity as end
Kingdom of ends
Good will

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
